question: What does Lock do?
answer: Lock creates one Google Sheet per binome in the Binome Sheets folder, shares it with both members (unless test mode is on) and starts routing new registrants to the binomes. From then on nobody is paired automatically: changes go through Change members. It can take up to five minutes for 50 binomes; if it stops early, press Lock again and it finishes the rest.

question: Can I redraw the binomes?
answer: Yes, until you lock. Draft pairs team members at random, an HR member with someone from another department, and writes them to the Binomes tab as drafts. Edit them freely in the sheet or redraw; a redraw replaces the current drafts and your edits to them. Locked binomes are never touched.

question: What does Import team replace?
answer: Import team reads the OT list into the Team tab. If the tab already holds members you are asked first, because the import replaces them and the Pair As and Exclude edits you made there are lost. Tick Exclude only for people who really will not interview.

question: What is test mode?
answer: While test mode is on, the script sends mail to the admins only and shares nothing, so the whole flow can be tried on the live Master without emailing the members. Turn it off at launch in Settings, Sharing and email; you are asked to confirm because real emails start going out.

question: How are registrants routed to binomes?
answer: IT, COMM and FLER registrants go to binomes of that department. HR registrants can go to any binome. The board binomes take anyone, and Settings, General can give them a lighter load. Every binome has an HR member.

question: Replace, swap or cover: which one?
answer: Replace is permanent: a member leaves, someone joins or the seat stays empty, and the leaver loses edit access to the sheet. Swap trades one member of each of two binomes in one step, and rolls both back if a write fails. Cover is temporary: a stand-in handles chosen candidates with view-only access, and the Binomes tab does not change.

question: A member has no binome after lock. What now?
answer: They appear as unpaired on the Binomes page. Press Place on their row to open Change members with their email filled in, choose the binome that has an empty seat and review. Nobody is paired automatically after lock because a redraw would reshuffle live binomes.

question: What does Move interviewee carry over?
answer: The candidate leaves one binome and joins another. Whether they were contacted, the interview date and the notes are carried to the new binome sheet. The new binome is emailed if new-interviewee emails are on.

question: How do I change a binome's department?
answer: Binomes, ⋯, Change department: tick the departments it receives (IT, COMM, FLER, HR). The preview shows the old and new tag, warns when it does not fit the members, and lists the candidates the new tag no longer covers; they stay, each with a Move link. Apply repaints the binome sheet and logs it in Change history. The binome is not emailed. A Tag typed by hand in the Master gets Apply on its Edited by hand alert, which keeps the typed tag and does the same.

question: Why do the HR-only binomes get more HR candidates?
answer: For an HR candidate, a binome tagged only HR counts its load divided by the HR-only binome weight (Settings, General, 2.5 by default) and wins ties, so it takes about that many times the load of the lightest mixed binome. The card How HR candidates are shared shows the live loads and follows the weight before you save. A new weight only affects new candidates; nobody already assigned is moved.

question: What does screening hold back?
answer: With screening on (Settings, Screening), each new application gets a risk score from its why-answers. One that is only dots or a slash, a single word, or a non-answer such as "I don't know" is held: no binome, and a Waiting for review alert. Length alone never holds a short but sincere answer, and nothing is declined on the score without a person deciding.

question: How do I review a held application?
answer: Open its Waiting for review alert: the reading pane shows the risk, the reasons and every answer. Approve assigns it to a binome straight away, with the full time to contact it, and sends the applicant their confirmation (a held application gets none before). Decline takes it out. Both work on several alerts at once. Declined rows stay under Interviewees, Declined, where Restore puts one back to Unassigned.

question: What happens when a VIC member applies?
answer: Their email is matched against the members sheet linked in Settings, Screening, and the Team tab. They are declined silently and get no mail. The sheet is read at most every 30 minutes; Refresh now reads it at once. A member who already has a binome is not pulled out: a VIC member alert offers Decline. If the sheet can't be read, an alert says so and nobody is declined.

question: When do declined applicants hear back?
answer: Only when an admin presses Maintenance, Send rejections once recruitment closes. Each applicant declined at screening gets one polite email, never the VIC members, and you can edit the text first. Each one is marked as sent, so pressing it again reaches only those not emailed yet. In test mode one copy goes to you and nothing is marked. Interviewed candidates who were not accepted are not included.

question: Who sees My binome?
answer: Someone in a locked binome, or a live cover, who is not an editor of the Master gets My binome only: their candidates, statuses, open alerts and a link to their sheet. An admin who is in a binome keeps the dashboard and finds My binome under People. It opens only while they can open their binome sheet; admins set that in Binomes, ⋯, Sheet & dashboard access (No access, View or Edit).

question: What can View and Edit do?
answer: Edit access to the binome sheet lets you fill in the gold fields (contacted, interview day and time, done, rating, affectation, notes) and the interview form. View is read-only, and so is a cover. What one partner saves shows on the other's screen at their next refresh.

question: How do I fill the interview form here?
answer: On My binome, Fill interview form opens the candidate's own page. Their 1st choice starts on the registration's value and picks the department section, and a bar counts the required answers. A draft is kept in this browser until you submit. After that the button says Edit answers, and you can change them any time; if your partner saved meanwhile, their version loads and your draft is kept. View-only members and covers get the Google Form, prefilled with both codes.

question: What does an interview form fill in?
answer: At the next sync the answers reach the Interview Log and the candidate becomes Interviewed. Every interview form, from the dashboard or the Google Form, fills Rating (the average of the scores, one decimal) and Final Affectation (7ECHOH is written as Not accepted) when they are empty. An edit refills a cell only if it still holds what the form wrote, so a value typed by hand stays.

question: How long may a candidate wait before an alert?
answer: Three limits, all counted from the moment the candidate was assigned: not contacted, no interview date, and no interview form after the interview. They are editable in Settings, Alerts and timing. Candidates who waited for a binome are not instantly late.

question: What does 'Edited by hand' mean?
answer: Someone changed a tab of the Master directly, which can silently break sheets, sharing and history. Apply properly runs the matching tool so everything follows; Revert puts back the value the script had written; Accept as is keeps the change and stops flagging it. Typed Status values and a cleared Binome are put back automatically.

question: Do alerts go away on their own?
answer: Timing and sheet-check alerts close themselves when the problem is gone. Others, such as a mistyped code on an interview form, stay until you mark them resolved. Resolving only hides the alert; it does not fix the data.

question: What are pending changes?
answer: While the owner has them on (Settings, General), Resolve, Snooze, Mute, Unmute, Save settings and My binome fields are accepted at once and written into the sheet shortly after, as you. Until then only you see them, marked Pending. With the switch off, every save is a direct write: you wait while it reaches the sheet.

question: Why does a change say Not applied?
answer: The sheet changed in a way that undoes what you wanted, or the change could not be written in time, for instance because your access or sign-in ended first. Choose Keep the sheet's value, or Apply mine anyway to send it again. If the sheet already does what you wanted, nothing is shown.

question: What if I left before a change was dropped?
answer: A dropped change no page showed within five minutes is emailed to you. Your next visit opens a dialog that must be answered: Keep the sheet's value for all, or Apply all of mine. If it goes unanswered, the admins get an alert.

question: Who can sign in?
answer: Anyone with an @g.enp.edu.dz account who can edit the VIC Recruitment 2026 master sheet. The script runs as you, so Google decides what you may touch. Sign-ins last 48 hours, and signing back in within that window skips the permission screen. Only the owner of the Master can run Setup.

question: Why does it say View only or No access?
answer: View only means your account can open the Master but is not an editor. No access means it cannot open it at all. Switch to another ENP account, or ask an admin to add you as an editor of the Master.

question: What does Check integrity look at?
answer: It syncs, then opens every binome sheet: missing or extra rows, moved tabs, lost protection and who can edit. It also runs with the daily digest. It stops before Vercel's five-minute limit and picks up where it stopped the next time you press it.

question: Why did a long action stop early?
answer: Lock and Check integrity end in time for the five-minute limit of the web function, and say how far they got. Run the same action again to continue; nothing is done twice.
